 Only one complete page of Nbk 14 carries draft for To a Sky-Lark, p. 97 rev. The
fragment of draft is considered in relation to the poem’s development to its final state in
Rogers (1967) 206–10. The ten pages following have been torn from the nbk, but words
and phrases on some of the remaining stubs indicate that more of the poem, perhaps
all of it, was drafted on the missing pages. S. transcribed a fair copy into Harvard Nbk
1, from which the press copy that was posted to Peacock on 12 July was taken, probably
by Mary, with only a few minor alterations of substance.
